name: Hardy–Weinberg inheritance equilibrium
description: Independent mathematical analyses by Weinberg and Hardy showed how inherited variants can retain stable proportions under idealized population assumptions.

date.label: 13 January 1908
date.basis: Dated lecture or publication, not the date of initial discovery.

events.statement: Weinberg presented an independent equilibrium analysis in Stuttgart in January 1908.

evidence.supports: Historical article dates Weinberg’s independent presentation to January 1908.

earliest_record.rationale: Dated witness within the inspected evidence; not a global-priority claim.

caveats: These are idealized population results, not a claim that real populations never evolve; earlier contributors also studied such proportions. Stern’s later account translates part of Weinberg’s published lecture; the indexed 2008 historical article was blocked at direct access.

research.note: Independent review checked the lecture and publication dates against Stern’s 1943 article and Hardy’s original letter; other facets retain their prior status.

links.statement: Hardy explicitly addressed the implications of Mendelian inheritance in his 1908 analysis.
